MRK.rationale: Merck's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe deterioration in fundamental health. The company reported a net loss of $4.24B (EPS -$1.72) versus net income of $5.08B (EPS $2.01) in Q1 2025, driven by a $9.0B one-time Cidara acquisition charge. While revenue grew 4.9% YoY to $16.29B, operating income swung to -$3.53B from +$5.90B, and operating margin collapsed to -21.7% from 37.8%. The GAAP gross margin fell to 74.2% from 78.0%. Operating cash flow declined 49.9% QoQ to $3.92B. The balance sheet shows total equity declining from $51.91B (Sep 2025) to $45.93B, while total liabilities increased to $82.75B. Valuation is extremely stretched: the P/E ratio has surged to 31.4x from a 12-month range of 10.8-15.8x, and P/B has risen to 6.1x from a range of 3.9-5.8x, all while earnings power has deteriorated. The Keytruda patent cliff (2028) remains the dominant structural risk, with the drug accounting for ~49% of FY2025 sales. Gardasil sales declined 24% in Q3 2025 due to China inventory issues. The company faces $2.5B in projected 2026 headwinds from generic competition and Medicare pricing pressures. Insider selling has been substantial, with the CMO and EVP reducing positions by 12.4% and 63.8% respectively. The stock has declined 4%%%%9%%%3.41 from $119.24, yet remains expensive on every metric. No credible near-term re-rating catalyst exists visible to could offset these deteriorating fundamentalsamentals and stretched valuation.
